job.style: a passage that shows a common wrong method and corrects it

passage: In our class data project, we recorded the number of books read by students: 0, 5, 5, 8, 10, and 12. To find the mean, we must include every observation, even the zero, because it represents a student who read no books. We add these values to get 40 and divide by the total count of 6, resulting in a mean of 6.67. Some students mistakenly think the mean must be one of the original numbers, but it is often a decimal. When finding the median for an even number of observations, we must take the average of the two middle values, which are 5 and 8. Adding them gives 13, and dividing by 2 results in a median of 6.5. A common error is picking the larger middle value, but the correct method requires averaging them. Furthermore, we identified the mode as 5, because it is the value that appears most frequently. Some students incorrectly claim the mode is 3, confusing the frequency of the value with the value itself. Finally, when drawing our bar graph, we noticed the scale intervals were 2 units each, not 1, showing that we must always check the axis labels carefully rather than assuming a standard unit gap.

items.evidence: To find the mean, we must include every observation, even the zero, because it represents a student who read no books.
items.q: Meena leaves out the 0 when finding the mean number of books. Why is she wrong?
options: The 0 is a real student who read nothing
The 0 should be counted as one book read
The 0 makes the total sum much bigger
The 0 is the most common value in the list
items.explain: The zero stands for a student who read no books, so that student must be counted.

wrong.why: thinks a zero entry means one item
thinks adding zero changes the sum
mixes up the mode with other values in the data

items.evidence: Some students mistakenly think the mean must be one of the original numbers, but it is often a decimal.
items.q: Asha gets a mean of 6.67, but 6.67 is not in the data. Is her answer right?
options: It is right; a mean is often a decimal
It is wrong; a mean must be in the list
It is wrong; divide by the 5 different values
It is right, because it equals the median
items.explain: The mean need not be one of the numbers; it is often a decimal like 6.67.

wrong.why: thinks the mean must be one of the data values
divides by the number of different values
mixes up the mean (6.67) with the median (6.5)

items.evidence: A common error is picking the larger middle value, but the correct method requires averaging them.
items.q: Ravi says the median of 0, 5, 5, 8, 10, 12 is 8. What mistake did he make?
options: He took one middle value instead of averaging both
He used the middle of an unsorted list
He forgot to count the zero as a value
He chose the value that appears most often
items.explain: With six values, the median is the average of 5 and 8, which is 6.5, not 8.

wrong.why: thinks median is taken in the given order
thinks the zero is left out of the data
mixes up the median with the mode

items.evidence: Furthermore, we identified the mode as 5, because it is the value that appears most frequently.
items.q: What makes 5 the mode of the books data?
options: It appears more times than any other value
It is the highest value in the data
It is the middle value in the given order
It is the value closest to the mean
items.explain: The mode is the value that occurs most often; 5 appears more than any other value.

wrong.why: thinks the mode is the highest value
confuses the mode with the median
confuses the mode with the mean

items.evidence: Finally, when drawing our bar graph, we noticed the scale intervals were 2 units each, not 1, showing that we must always check the axis labels carefully rather than assuming a standard unit gap.
items.q: On the class bar graph, a bar reaches 5 gaps up the scale. How many books does it show?
options: 10 books, since each gap is 2 units
5 books, since each gap is 1 unit
7 books, adding the 2 to the 5 gaps
6 books, counting the zero line as a gap
items.explain: Each scale gap stands for 2 units, so 5 gaps show 5 × 2 = 10 books.

wrong.why: adds the interval instead of multiplying
miscounts the gaps on the scale
